definition: OMI is an open-source AI pendant that listens to conversations and makes them searchable later. Hardware sells from $129 to $179.
extendedDescription:
OMI takes the open route to wearables. The hardware listens throughout your day, and the open-source software turns those conversations into a searchable record you control.

Because it is open source, you can inspect what it does with your audio and run parts of it yourself. That transparency is rare in a category built on always-on microphones.

Capture is only half the job. OMI remembers what was said. It does not draft the follow-up email, create the task, or update the calendar. Recall without action still leaves you the to-do list.

faqs.answer: OMI hardware sells from $129 to $179 depending on the model. The software is open source.

howGaiaUsesIt: GAIA respects the open-source ethos and shares it: GAIA is fully open source and self-hostable via Docker. Where OMI stops at recall, GAIA continues into action, turning captured context into drafted emails, created tasks, and scheduled events across 50+ integrations.
